content: The University of Michigan Health System (UMHS) is a fully integrated academic medical center owned by the University of Michigan, located in Ann Arbor. It encompasses several key facilities, including the C.S. Mott Children’s Hospital, Women’s Hospital, numerous outpatient clinics, and the Michigan Visiting Nurses program. UMHS also operates the Michigan Health Corporation, which collaborates with other medical centers and hospitals across Michigan to deliver specialized care. Additionally, UMHS has partnered with Blue Cross Blue Shield of Michigan in a joint venture called Michigan Health Quarters, established in 2007 to focus on healthcare quality research and transformation. UMHS has set a strategic goal of achieving a 3% annual operating margin over the next decade to support its extensive facility expansion projects. As a not-for-profit entity, UMHS reinvests its positive operating margins into advancing patient care, education, research, and the infrastructure necessary to sustain these functions. The health system is renowned for its comprehensive and high-quality care, with specialized centers dedicated to conditions such as Alzheimer’s disease, cancer, cardiovascular care, depression, diabetes, epilepsy, geriatrics, organ transplantation, pediatrics, trauma/burn care, vision, and women’s health. Its hospitals collectively house 961 licensed beds, with plans to add nearly 300 more by 2011. UMHS is a major tertiary care center, boasting 179 intensive care unit (ICU) beds, one of the highest numbers in the nation, and 66 operating rooms, which will increase to 82 with the completion of new construction projects, including the $523 million Children and Women’s Hospital and the $132 million Eye Center expansion. Outpatient care is provided at the main medical campus in Ann Arbor and at various satellite locations. The Michigan Visiting Nurses program offers a wide range of home care services, including nursing, specialty treatments, therapy, palliative care, and immunization services, across a 13-county area in southeastern Michigan. UMHS also operates a medical evacuation program called Survival Flight, which includes three helicopters and a Cessna jet, transporting critically ill patients from Michigan, Ohio, Ontario, and beyond to Ann Arbor for advanced care. The UMHS Medical School faculty comprises all 1,600 physicians who treat UM patients. The school trains 683 medical students, 1,010 interns and residents, 503 graduate students, and 482 postdoctoral research fellows. It also provides continuing medical education to over 15,000 practicing physicians and health professionals annually. The Medical School is affiliated with the VA Ann Arbor Healthcare System, where UM faculty physicians provide care and students receive training. UMHS is undergoing one of the largest expansions of any hospital system in the nation, with several major building projects completed or underway. These include the Ambulatory Surgery and Medical Procedures Center, the Biomedical Science Research Building, the Upjohn Depression Center, and the Cardiovascular Center. Future projects include the Kellogg Eye/Brehm Diabetes Center, the new Mott Children’s and Women’s Hospital, and facilities for cardiovascular research, musculoskeletal care, emergency health services, and health education. UMHS is consistently ranked among the nation’s top medical and research institutions, receiving numerous awards for its advanced medical care, cutting-edge biomedical research, and extensive educational activities. It is recognized for excellence in specialties such as ear, nose, and throat; neurology and neurosurgery; orthopedics; heart and heart surgery; cancer; ophthalmology; and urology. The system has also been acknowledged for its high-quality, safe, effective, and equitable patient care. The main medical campus includes the University Hospital, which opened in 1986 and houses 794 beds, 33 operating rooms, and specialized care programs such as the Level I Adult Trauma Center, the Michigan Trauma-Burn Unit, the Michigan Transplant Center, the Michigan Comprehensive Epilepsy Center, and the Michigan Stroke Center. The C.S. Mott Children’s Hospital, which opened in 1969, provides inpatient care for children and adolescents, including a 15-bed Child & Adolescent Psychiatry unit and a 40-bed Neonatal Intensive Care Unit. The new Mott Children’s and Women’s Hospital, set to open in 2011, will feature two towers with 264 inpatient beds, 16 operating rooms, and specialized centers such as the Michigan Congenital Heart Center and the Holden Neonatal Intensive Care Unit. The Kellogg Eye Center, a world-renowned facility for adult and pediatric eye care, is undergoing a $132 million expansion to include new clinic space, surgical suites, and research facilities. The Comprehensive Cancer Center, opened in 1997, is a nine-story facility dedicated to outpatient cancer care and research, with specialized clinics for adrenal cancer, gynecologic oncology, and more. The Cardiovascular Center, opened in 2007, provides state-of-the-art care for adults with cardiovascular disease and includes 48 inpatient beds, eight operating rooms, and 11 interventional procedure suites. UMHS also features the Biomedical Science Research Building, a six-story facility housing 472,000 square feet of research space, and the Life Sciences Institute, which supports interdisciplinary research in areas such as nanotechnology, neuroscience, and regenerative medicine. The system’s facilities include the Taubman Medical Library, the Towsley Center for Continuing Medical Education, and the Med Inn Building, which provides accommodations for families of critically ill patients. UMHS is a leader in research, with the Medical School ranking 10th nationally in NIH funding, receiving $265 million annually. The system’s research budget exceeds $333 million, supporting groundbreaking work in areas such as cancer, cardiovascular disease, and neuroscience.
